learningObjectives.title: The meaning and observance of festivals

questions.q: During which month of the Islamic calendar do Muslims observe Sawm (fasting)?
questions.explain: Sawm is the obligatory fast kept throughout the month of Ramadan, the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.

questions.q: What is the name of the meal Muslims eat before dawn during Ramadan?
questions.explain: Suhur is the pre-dawn meal taken before the fast begins each day of Ramadan.

questions.q: What is the name of the meal that breaks the daily fast at sunset?
questions.explain: Iftar is the meal eaten at sunset to break the day's fast, often begun with dates and water.

questions.q: Which Pillar of Islam is fulfilled by fasting during Ramadan?
questions.explain: Sawm, fasting during Ramadan, is one of the Five Pillars of Islam.

questions.q: Between which two times of day do Muslims fast during Ramadan?
questions.explain: The daily fast lasts from dawn (before Fajr prayer) until sunset (Maghrib).

questions.q: What is the name of the special night during Ramadan when the revelation of the Qur'an began?
questions.explain: Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Power, marks when the Qur'an first began to be revealed to Muhammad.

questions.q: Which festival marks the end of the month of Ramadan?
questions.explain: Id-ul-Fitr is celebrated on the first day of Shawwal to mark the end of Ramadan's fasting.

questions.q: Which prophet's willingness to sacrifice his son is commemorated at Id-ul-Adha?
questions.explain: Id-ul-Adha recalls Ibrahim's readiness to sacrifice his son in obedience to Allah, who provided a ram instead.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains a purpose of fasting during Ramadan?
options: To develop self-discipline and empathy for the poor
To lose weight for health reasons
To prove physical strength to others
questions.explain: Sawm teaches self-control, obedience to Allah and compassion for those who go without food.

questions.q: What does the name 'Id-ul-Fitr' mean?
questions.explain: Id-ul-Fitr means the Festival of Breaking the Fast, celebrated at the close of Ramadan.

questions.q: What does the name 'Id-ul-Adha' mean?
questions.explain: Id-ul-Adha means the Festival of Sacrifice, commemorating Ibrahim's obedience to Allah.

questions.q: Why is Laylat al-Qadr regarded as especially significant by Muslims?
options: It marks the beginning of the Qur'an's revelation to Muhammad
It is the day Id-ul-Adha is celebrated
It marks the birth of Muhammad
It is when the Ka'bah was built
questions.explain: The Night of Power is when the Qur'an began to be revealed, described as better than a thousand months.

questions.q: At Id-ul-Adha, how is the meat of the sacrificed animal traditionally shared?
options: Into three parts: for the family, for relatives and friends, and for the poor
It is all given to the mosque
It is all kept by the family
It is all sold at market
questions.explain: The Qurbani meat is divided into three shares so that the poor are also included in the festival.

questions.q: Which group is normally permitted an exemption from fasting during Ramadan?
options: People who are travelling for leisure by choice
questions.explain: The sick, travellers, the very young, the elderly, and pregnant or menstruating women may be exempt from fasting.

questions.q: Why do many Muslims give Zakat-ul-Fitr before the Id-ul-Fitr prayer?
options: So that poorer Muslims can also share in the celebration
To pay for the mosque building
questions.explain: Zakat-ul-Fitr is a charitable gift given before the Id prayer so that the needy can enjoy the festival too.

questions.q: Which of these is a common way Muslims observe Id-ul-Fitr?
options: Attending special congregational prayers and wearing new clothes
Avoiding all food for the whole day
questions.explain: Id-ul-Fitr is marked by communal prayers, new clothes, sweet foods, visiting family and giving to charity.

questions.q: Aisha is pregnant and her doctor advises that fasting could harm her health. According to Islamic teaching, what may she do during Ramadan?
options: She may be excused from fasting and make up the days later or feed the poor
She must fast regardless of her health
She must never fast again in her life
She must complete the Hajj instead
questions.explain: Pregnant women may be exempt and can make up the missed days later or provide meals for the needy.

questions.q: A family shares dates and water at sunset, then eats a larger meal together, during the month of fasting. Which observance is this?
questions.explain: It is customary to break the daily Ramadan fast at Iftar, traditionally beginning with dates and water.

questions.q: During the days of the Hajj, a family sacrifices a sheep and distributes its meat to relatives and the poor. Which festival are they observing?
questions.explain: Id-ul-Adha, the Festival of Sacrifice, falls during the days of Hajj and involves the Qurbani sacrifice.

questions.q: At the end of Ramadan, a Muslim boy puts on new clothes, gives a charitable gift, and attends congregational prayers before enjoying sweet foods with family. Which festival is he celebrating?
questions.explain: These joyful customs of new clothes, charity, prayers and sweet foods are typical of Id-ul-Fitr.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Religious Studies (0490) syllabus; Islam: Festivals & Fasts
